title: Semantic Punning (Artificial Method Consistency)
pattern: Using the exact same method name (e.g., `add`) for fundamentally different mathematical or collection operations simply to maintain superficial consistency.
why_bad: It creates a semantic pun. Callers expect methods sharing a name to behave similarly. Using `add` for "insert into a collection" and "mathematical sum" misleads developers regarding side-effects, computational complexity, and mathematical invariants.
detection: A method named `add` that inserts or appends items to a collection instead of performing mathematical accumulation, while other modules use `add` for mathematical summation.
counterexample: Standard library traits (like `std::ops::Add`) where the implementation strictly obeys the mathematical properties of addition.
